campbell.title: Campbell City Council — July 7, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered renewing an interim ordinance related to state Senate Bill implementation, along with two separate hearings on revoking the business license and tobacco retailer permit for California Cigar and for Hayes Smoke Shop. The council also considered authorizing a grant application for public works funding and approving new consultant service agreements.
keyTopics: Renewal of an interim ordinance implementing a state Senate Bill
Revocation of business license and tobacco retailer permit for California Cigar
Revocation of business license and tobacco retailer permit for Hayes Smoke Shop
Authorization to submit a grant application through the Public Works Department
Approval of consultant service agreements

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — May 20, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council considered a resolution declaring the City's intent to identify certain designated properties, likely as an early step in a formal city process. The Council also set a public hearing for June 17, 2026, where residents can raise protests and the Council will consider final approval of the matter.
keyTopics: Resolution declaring intent to identify designated properties
Scheduling of a public hearing on June 17, 2026
Process for residents to file protests before final approval
Next steps toward final Council decision on the designated properties

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — August 4, 2026
los-gatos.summary: At this meeting, the Los Gatos Town Council considered routine housekeeping items, including approval of minutes from prior meetings and several contract amendments for ongoing services like tree care and legal counsel. The Council also considered authorizing the annual purchase of library books and materials, and reviewed the Town's monthly financial and investment report.
keyTopics: Approval of minutes from the June 16 and June 23, 2026 Council meetings
Contract amendments for tree care services with Brightview
Amendment to the Town's legal services contract
Authorization to purchase library books and materials through Ingram for the fiscal year
Monthly financial and investment report review

san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — August 5, 2026
san-jose.summary: This was an administrative planning meeting where city staff and council leadership finalized the agenda for the August 11, 2026 City Council meeting and reviewed a draft agenda for the August 18, 2026 meeting. They also reviewed the public record covering city business from June 11 to July 29, 2026.
keyTopics: Finalizing items for the August 11, 2026 Council meeting agenda
Reviewing and shaping the draft agenda for August 18, 2026
Considering whether any agenda items need a scheduled 'time certain' for discussion
Checking agenda items and documents for required public notice waivers
Reviewing the public record log covering June 11 through July 29, 2026

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — June 23, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View City Council met to discuss city finances and infrastructure, including setting next year's spending limits, updating budget policy, and reviewing a long-term water management plan. The council also considered several construction and repair projects, including work on the Public Safety Building, Shoreline Golf Links parking lot, and a South Bay salt pond restoration effort, plus a closed-door legal session on potential lawsuits against the city.
keyTopics: Closed session on potential litigation against the city
Proclamations for Immigrant Heritage Month, the Kiwanis Club's 100th anniversary, and City Attorney Jennifer Logue's judicial appointment
Setting the city's legal spending limit and updating budget policy for next fiscal year
Adoption of the 5-year water supply and drought planning update
Capital projects covering the Public Safety Building, Shoreline Golf Links parking lot repaving, and South Bay salt pond restoration

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — July 28, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: On July 28, 2026, the Sunnyvale City Council held a special meeting that began with a closed-door session, followed by a public study session focused on artificial turf. During the study session, the Council considered an update on the city's policy regarding the use of artificial turf on athletic fields and other public spaces.
keyTopics: Closed session held before the public portion of the meeting
Study session on the city's Artificial Turf Policy
Update on considerations for artificial turf use on fields and public grounds

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — August 4, 2026
cupertino.summary: This Cupertino City Council meeting opened with standard procedural items, including any postponements to the agenda and time set aside for public comment. Residents were given the opportunity to speak to the Council about topics not otherwise listed on the agenda, with each speaker limited to three minutes.
keyTopics: Announcements of any postponements or changes to the agenda order
Public comment period for non-agenda items (Oral Communications)
Time limits on public speakers (three minutes each, thirty minutes total)
Additional public comment allowed later in the meeting after the City Manager's report

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara Station Area Task Force — July 16, 2026
santa-clara.summary: This Santa Clara City Council meeting agenda included the standard legal disclosure that accompanies council meetings, explaining the deadline residents have to challenge certain city decisions in court. Specific policy items for this meeting were not detailed beyond this procedural notice.
keyTopics: Standard notice on legal challenge deadlines for city decisions
90-day filing window under Code of Civil Procedure Section 1094.6
Rules governing quasi-adjudicative decisions made by the City

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — August 3, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council considered a resolution to place a Business Tax Modernization Measure on the ballot, which would shift the city's business tax from its current structure to a tiered gross receipts system. The proposal was framed as a way to more fairly tax businesses based on actual economic activity while protecting smaller businesses from higher costs.
keyTopics: Resolution to place a business tax modernization measure on the ballot
Switching to a tiered gross receipts tax structure
Protections for small businesses, most of which have limited annual revenue
Comparing Milpitas's business tax revenue to other cities in the region
Simplifying tax administration and adapting to changes in the modern economy

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto City Council — June 29, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto City Council held a public hearing on a proposal at 2468 South Court to tear down an existing one-story house and detached garage and replace them with a new two-story, 2,481-square-foot single-family home that includes a 1,512-square-foot basement. Because this involved a Director's Review of a tentative approval, the Council acted in a quasi-judicial role, weighing whether the project meets the city's design and zoning rules for this R-1 single-family neighborhood.
keyTopics: Director's Review appeal of a tentative approval for a house rebuild at 2468 South Court
Demolition of an existing single-story home and detached garage
Plans for a new two-story residence with a basement and an attached JADU (junior accessory dwelling unit)
Compliance with R-1 single-family zoning standards
Project's exemption from further environmental review under CEQA rules
